newsitem.title: USA: Gore warns Republicans on budget deal.
newsitem.headline: Gore warns Republicans on budget deal.

text.p: Vice President Al Gore warned Republican congressional leaders Saturday that President Clinton would "hold their feet to the fire" on the budget agreement just as he did on disaster relief aid.
"The president held their feet to the fire (in passing disaster relief) and they ended up doing the right thing," Gore told about 50 supporters at a $5,000 a-person fundraiser.
He said that some Republican leaders had violated the bipartisan agreement on passing a balanced budget acceptable to the Clinton administration.
"But there is still time for them to keep their word and I predict that they will," the vice president added.

Addressing his audience in a 19th floor dining room with a sweeping view of Cincinnati's Ohio Riverfront, he backhandedly praised the Republican leadership for "coming to their senses" on disaster aid.

After originally passing a disaster relief bill with provisions that Clinton found objectionable and vetoed, Congress acted swiftly and overwhelmingly enacted a $5.6 billion relief measure on Thursday.

Gore noted that he had come to Cincinnati in March when the area was besieged with the worst Ohio River flood in three decades and promised speedy financial relief for flood victims. The disaster relief bill that was passed contained $355 million for the Ohio-Kentucky-Indiana area.

To maintain the nation's current healthy economy, the vice president called for continued efforts to reduce the deficit and balance the budget while making room for adequate funding for education, the environment and technology. He also called for the opening of new overseas markets for U.S. products.

After his talk, Gore briefly visited an "Italian Street Festival" in nearby Newport, Ky., for a photo-opportunity session with the public before flying on to Columbus, Ohio, for a Saturday evening Democratic fundraiser honouring retiring Democratic Senator John Glenn.
